globalBoundary: Camera metrics describe a recorded movement strategy. They do not diagnose pathology, identify a weak or tight muscle, measure passive joint mobility, or measure fascial-line loading.

crossViewContract.boundary: Side and front recordings are analysed independently. Cross-view synthesis groups view-specific observations by theme but does not synchronize repetitions, average view-specific angles, or upgrade proxies into diagnosis.

fascialLineContext.name: Superficial Back Line
fascialLineContext.anatomicalContinuity: plantar foot, calf complex, hamstring region, sacral fascia, and spinal extensor region
fascialLineContext.squatContext: May provide anatomical context for heel behavior, ankle strategy, selected depth, posterior hip contribution, and sagittal trunk support.
fascialLineContext.boundary: The camera does not measure SBL tension, restriction, recoil, or loading.

dynamicSwitch.name: Calcaneal Station Elevation & Knee Switch
dynamicSwitch.failureMode: Soleus/Achilles terminal length locks ankle, forcing calcaneal elevation bypass.

fascialLineContext.retestProtocol: Elevate heels on 15-20mm wedge. If squat depth and upright trunk normalize, confirms distal SBL/Achilles block.

prescriptionTriad.release: Deep tissue myofascial release along gastrocnemius-soleus junction & suboccipitals (2 min)
prescriptionTriad.activate: Tibialis anterior isometric dorsiflexion + deep neck flexor nods
prescriptionTriad.integrate: Goblet box squat maintaining heel-tripod contact

fascialLineContext.name: Superficial Front Line
fascialLineContext.anatomicalContinuity: anterior lower leg, quadriceps region, anterior trunk, and front of the neck
fascialLineContext.squatContext: May provide anatomical context for knee-extension contribution, tibial organization, and anterior trunk support in the side view.
fascialLineContext.boundary: The camera does not measure SFL activation, shortness, restriction, or loading.

dynamicSwitch.name: ASIS Pelvic Station Anchor Switch
dynamicSwitch.failureMode: Rectus Femoris pulls ASIS downward as Transversus/Rectus Abdominis fails to anchor pelvis.

fascialLineContext.retestProtocol: Perform squat while holding a light anterior load (Goblet position) with active core bracing cue.

prescriptionTriad.release: Rectus femoris and anterior hip flexor foam rolling / trigger point release
prescriptionTriad.activate: Dead bug with neutral pelvic tilt + VMO terminal knee extension
prescriptionTriad.integrate: Tempo pause squats with vertical torso focus

fascialLineContext.name: Deep Front Line
fascialLineContext.anatomicalContinuity: inner foot and deep lower leg, adductor region, pelvic floor, psoas region, and deep trunk continuity
fascialLineContext.squatContext: May provide anatomical context for medial foot-knee organization, adductor-pelvis relationships, depth strategy, and trunk-pelvis support across views.
fascialLineContext.boundary: The camera does not measure DFL support, tension, restriction, or force transmission.

dynamicSwitch.name: Femoral Adductor Switch & Medial Arch Stirrup
dynamicSwitch.failureMode: Adductor Magnus / Longus pulls femur into medial rotation and arch collapses at peak depth.

fascialLineContext.retestProtocol: Place mini-band above knees and cue active tripod short-foot grounding during descent.

prescriptionTriad.release: Adductor magnus & longus deep ischemic compression along medial thigh
prescriptionTriad.activate: Short-foot tripod activation + side-lying clamshell with glute med focus
prescriptionTriad.integrate: Band-resisted squats ensuring knees track over 2nd toe

fascialLineContext.name: Lateral Line
fascialLineContext.anatomicalContinuity: lateral foot and lower leg, iliotibial region, lateral pelvis, lateral trunk, and neck
fascialLineContext.squatContext: May provide anatomical context for pelvic shift, trunk shift, stance organization, and frontal-plane asymmetry in the front view.
fascialLineContext.boundary: The camera does not measure Lateral Line balance, restriction, stiffness, or loading.

dynamicSwitch.name: Lateral Harness & Pelvic Shelf Switch
dynamicSwitch.failureMode: Quadratus Lumborum hikes pelvis as stance gluteus medius fails to stabilize frontal plane.

fascialLineContext.retestProtocol: Perform supported single-leg split squat to evaluate unilateral frontal-plane hip control.

prescriptionTriad.release: TFL / ITB junction and quadratus lumborum soft tissue release
prescriptionTriad.activate: Side plank hip abduction + banded lateral monster walks
prescriptionTriad.integrate: Single-leg Romanian deadlift to squat pattern transition

fascialLineContext.name: Spiral Line
fascialLineContext.anatomicalContinuity: cross-body foot, leg, pelvis, abdominal, thoracic, and shoulder-girdle continuities
fascialLineContext.squatContext: May provide anatomical context when knee-to-foot, pelvis, and trunk observations suggest a coupled frontal or rotational image-plane strategy.
fascialLineContext.boundary: The camera cannot isolate transverse-plane rotation or measure Spiral Line restriction or loading.

dynamicSwitch.name: Asymmetric Transverse Sling Switch
dynamicSwitch.failureMode: Cross-body obliques and deep hip rotators torque pelvis over femur during depth transition.

fascialLineContext.retestProtocol: Align feet facing 0° forward and perform seated thoracic rotation test to isolate trunk vs hip rotational asymmetry.

prescriptionTriad.release: Biceps femoris lateral tendon and contralateral oblique myofascial release
prescriptionTriad.activate: Seated thoracic rotation with isometric pelvic block
prescriptionTriad.integrate: Offset dumbbell front squat with rotational stabilization

superficial_back_line.whyObserved: Heel rise, limited comfortable depth, a hip-dominant strategy, or posterior trunk bracing may indicate a posterior sagittal organisation worth investigating.
superficial_back_line.muscleLineRelationship: Calf and plantar-foot tissues, hamstrings, gluteus maximus, sacral continuity, and spinal extensors may contribute to a coordinated posterior strategy.
potentialIssues: calf strategy limiting forward tibial progression
altered hamstring or gluteus maximus timing
superficial_back_line.assessmentQuestion: Compare heel support, stance, ankle options, and active hip-extension control, then retest whether the depth or trunk strategy changes.

superficial_front_line.whyObserved: A knee-dominant trunk-tibia relationship or anterior trunk organisation may bring the anterior chain into consideration.
superficial_front_line.muscleLineRelationship: Tibialis anterior and the anterior lower leg relate to quadriceps and anterior trunk continuity in the organisation of knee progression, knee extension, and trunk control.
superficial_front_line.assessmentQuestion: Change foot position and depth, assess quadriceps, hip-flexor, and anterior-ankle options, then retest with hip or trunk cueing.

deep_front_line.whyObserved: Medial knee drift, medial foot collapse, or difficulty maintaining the inner foot and pelvis relationship may bring the deep medial chain into consideration.
deep_front_line.muscleLineRelationship: Deep foot and lower-leg contributors, adductors, pelvic-floor and psoas region, and deep trunk support may organise the medial relationship between foot, knee, pelvis, and trunk.
potentialIssues: adductor stiffness or poor adductor contribution
deep_front_line.assessmentQuestion: Assess foot tripod and arch control, adductor length and contraction, hip-rotation options, and whether a medial-chain cue changes the knee path.

lateral_line.whyObserved: Pelvic or trunk shift, repeated asymmetrical loading, wide-stance dependence, or outward knee drift may indicate a lateral balance strategy.
lateral_line.muscleLineRelationship: Lateral foot and lower leg, tensor fasciae latae and IT region, gluteus medius, lateral abdominal wall, and quadratus lumborum may coordinate frontal-plane organisation.
lateral_line.assessmentQuestion: Check stance symmetry, compare supported and narrow-stance versions, assess lateral hip and trunk control, and retest pelvis-over-foot organisation.

spiral_line.whyObserved: Foot rotation coupled with knee-to-foot tracking, pelvic rotation or shift, and trunk or shoulder orientation may indicate a diagonal rotational strategy.
spiral_line.muscleLineRelationship: Tibialis anterior and peroneus longus relate foot orientation to the lower limb; biceps femoris long head relates the posterolateral thigh toward the pelvis; obliques relate pelvis to rib cage; serratus anterior and rhomboids relate trunk to shoulder girdle.
potentialIssues: serratus anterior or rhomboid coordination problem
spiral_line.assessmentQuestion: Test foot angle and tibial rotation options, compare pelvis and thorax control independently, assess oblique and scapular coordination, and retest after changing the setup.

entries.title: Trunk-tibia relationship
entries.observationTemplate: The trunk-tibia angle at maximum depth was {value} degrees.
entries.strategyInterpretation: Values above 10 degrees are described as relatively hip-extensor biased, values from -10 to 10 degrees as neutral, and values below -10 degrees as relatively knee-extensor biased.

entries.title: Selected squat depth
entries.strategyInterpretation: Depth reflects a combined ankle-knee-hip strategy and the task setup. The review groups 0-90 degrees as shallow, 90-110 degrees as medium, and 110-135 degrees as deep.

entries.title: Heel-rise observation
entries.observationTemplate: Heel elevation relative to the forefoot baseline was {value} normalized units.
entries.strategyInterpretation: The ankle-foot strategy may not have accommodated the selected depth while the starting foot position was maintained.

entries.title: Knee-to-foot tracking
entries.observationTemplate: The knee moved medially or laterally relative to the foot proxy during {phase}.
entries.strategyInterpretation: Hip, knee, ankle-foot, stance, and camera factors should be reviewed together.
candidateMuscleRegions: tensor fasciae latae and IT region
deep lower-leg and foot stabilizer regions

entries.title: Pelvic lateral shift
entries.observationTemplate: Pelvis midpoint moved {direction} by {value} normalized units relative to standing baseline.
entries.strategyInterpretation: This describes an asymmetric frontal-plane pelvis strategy during the recorded squat and does not identify its cause.

entries.title: Trunk shift relative to pelvis
entries.observationTemplate: The shoulder midpoint shifted {direction} relative to the pelvis by {value} normalized units.
entries.strategyInterpretation: This describes frontal-plane trunk-pelvis organization in the recording, not spinal or hip dysfunction.

entries.title: Left-right frontal contribution
entries.observationTemplate: Left-right knee-depth contribution differed by {value} normalized units at maximum pelvis descent.
entries.strategyInterpretation: The two sides contributed differently in the image plane during this recording; the proxy cannot identify a weaker or restricted side.

entries.title: Repetition consistency
entries.observationTemplate: Across {count} repetitions, peak-depth variability was {value} degrees.
entries.strategyInterpretation: This describes how repeatable the recorded strategy was under this protocol.
